summary: The launch-fusion idea is plausible, but the change quietly bundles a second sub-change. The sorted_ids/block_experts capacity drops from SGLang's 256-expert sizing to 32-expert sizing, which changes the m-block count Marlin's persistent scheduler partitions over. Run it with one in-run control that keeps the new kernel but allocates SGLang's 256-expert capacity, so the launch effect and the capacity effect can be told apart.
justification: Mechanism: at T<=32 the parent branch (expert-id-map-single-kernel) issues the id-map kernel plus SGLang's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, bsm, 256). With num_experts=256 the sgl op cannot take its small-batch single-kernel path (that path needs few experts), so it issues the multi-kernel path: align/cumsum, count-and-sort, and possibly a separate sorted_ids fill. Replacing 3-5 graph-replayed tiny kernels with one is plausible on H200 at ~1.5-2.5 us per back-to-back tiny kernel, and decode_1 (168-181 us, SoL 40-44 us) is launch-bound. Prior art: in muse_moe_w4a16, align-single-token-ep (one SGLang single-token align kernel at bs=1) measured +4.1% at decode_1 (80.2 -> 77.0 us), so a ~3 us align saving is real at T=1. Weakest links: (1) FINDINGS never shows the align kernels in any top-3 list, so the '8-10 us' saving is assumed, not measured. A realistic net is 3-7 us: 2-4% at decode_1, ~2% at verify_1, ~1-2% at decode_16 sliding, and decode_32 / decode_16 full (430-615 us) inside the per-shape noise. (2) The change says the buffers keep 'the host-sized capacity T*8 + 32*(block_size_m - 1) that SGLang would allocate for 32 experts'. But this pipeline, like baseline.py, calls moe_align_block_size with N_EXPERTS=256, so SGLang here allocates T*8 + 256*(bsm-1). Using bsm=8 for T in {1,8,16} and bsm=16 for T=32, the sizes are: T=1 1800 vs 232 slots (225 vs 29 m-blocks); T=8 1856 vs 288 (232 vs 36); T=16 1920 vs 352 (240 vs 44); T=32 4096 vs 736 (256 vs 46). Marlin MoE takes its parallel m-block count from sorted_ids.size(0)/moe_block_size on the host and stripes k/n tiles over that. So shrinking capacity can change Marlin's work partition and early-exit pattern, and Marlin is 22-42% of every T<=32 shape. That is exactly the queued moe-align-local-expert-count mechanism, bundled in here, and it could move Marlin in either direction. A hint it might cost something: muse_moe_w4a16's 32-count master was an unexplained 3.2 us slower than SGLang's 256-count path at bs=1. (3) A single-program Triton counting sort at T=32 (256 routes, per-expert ranks via a one-hot [256,32] cumsum or a [256,256] compare) is not free. It may run 2-4 us itself, which eats much of the saving at decode_32. The directions in `expected` agree with the shape weights: decode_* and verify_1 carry weight 46/16 per layer and verify_16/32 are correctly held as controls. The magnitudes are optimistic by about 2x.
confounders: expert-id-map-single-kernel (unpromoted parent, neutral 1.037x with uniform +1-2.5% drift on every shape): at T<=32 this hypothesis removes the parent's kernel, so the T<=32 delta versus BEST/master covers master's 3 id-map ops plus SGLang's align, collapsed to 1 kernel. At T=128/256 the parent's id-map kernel stays, so verify_16/verify_32 are not pure master controls. They carry the parent's 3->1 id-map change, worth ~0.5% at most on 500-1050 us shapes. Read them as drift controls with that small bias, and compare against the parent's result as well as against BEST.

sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (landed): it sets moe_align_block_size's num_experts=256 and the side-stream router/routing that joins before the expert block. The join happens before local_ids, so the fused kernel stays serial on the main stream exactly as the old align was. No overlap interaction. The router change itself touches only T=8 (verify_1), which is upstream of the align and unaffected. Not a real confounder, except that it fixes the 256-expert capacity this hypothesis silently changes.

Bundled sub-change (not a landed hypothesis, but the main confounder): the 256->32 expert capacity shrink alters Marlin's host-side m-block partition on every T<=32 shape. Without a control, a gain or loss cannot be pinned on launch removal versus a Marlin scheduling change. It also overlaps the queued moe-align-local-expert-count, which tests the same capacity change at large T on a different base and run.
interference: A companion is warranted. Without one, both outcomes are ambiguous. A gain at decode_1/verify_1 could come from fewer launches or from Marlin running fewer and differently partitioned m-block slices (225->29 at T=1). A flat or negative result could mean the fused kernel's own time offset the launch saving, or that the capacity shrink hurt Marlin while the fusion helped. Cross-run comparison with moe-align-local-expert-count will not resolve this: it runs on master rather than this branch, it mostly measures large T, and run-to-run drift in this problem is +-1.5-2.5% per shape (see expert-id-map's uniform shift), which matches the expected effect size. The fix is an in-run control on the same branch: the same single kernel, with sorted_ids and block_experts sized exactly as moe_align_block_size(..., 256) sizes them. Then the control minus the parent's result isolates launch fusion at identical Marlin inputs, and the primary minus the control isolates the capacity effect at small T. No ab-revert is needed. The parent's id-map kernel is subsumed at T<=32 anyway, and the landed router change does not interact.
rules_flags: The self-check described in Risk ('compare tensor-for-tensor against SGLang's op on the 13 tests' routings in prepare()') cannot use the tests' routings: prepare() only sees weights. Use synthetic topk_ids, such as random ids with fixed seeds for T in {1,8,16,32} and local_start in {0,32,224}, including all-remote and all-one-expert cases. Do not cache anything derived from data. Any print must be in prepare(), never in kernel_fn.

kernel_fn must not read num_tokens_post_pad or any count on the host. Grid and buffer sizes must come only from T (shape) and block_size_m. The single-program grid (1,) and fixed-capacity buffers satisfy this. Keep the T<=32 branch on num_tokens, which is a shape.

Warm-compile the Triton kernel in prepare() for every constexpr variant used (each BLOCK/bsm/T bucket), so no JIT happens during graph capture or timing. Do not add triton.autotune, which other problems' rules checklists forbid.
No precision issue: integer-only outputs. topk_weights, the Marlin calls and fp32 reduce are unchanged.

companions.change: Identical to moe-align-single-kernel-small-t (built on the expert-id-map-single-kernel branch: the same single-program Triton kernel at T <= 32 writing local_ids, sorted_ids, block_experts and num_tokens_post_pad, and the same T=128/256 fallback to SGLang's moe_align_block_size(local_ids, block_size_m, N_EXPERTS)) with one difference: at T <= 32 allocate sorted_ids with SGLang's 256-expert capacity, T*8 + N_EXPERTS*(block_size_m - 1) entries (1800/1856/1920 for T=1/8/16 at bsm 8, 4096 for T=32 at bsm 16). Allocate block_experts with cdiv(that capacity, block_size_m) entries (225/232/240/256), exactly as moe_align_block_size(..., 256) sizes them. The kernel still fills every unused sorted_ids slot with the numel sentinel (T*8) and every unused block_experts slot with -1. Only the extent of the two buffers grows. The device-side contents of the used prefix and num_tokens_post_pad are bit-identical to the primary's. Marlin, silu_and_mul, the post-expert sum and block_size_m selection are unchanged.

expected.why: Pure launch removal at SGLang-identical Marlin input shapes: ~3-6 us on ~170-180 us
Saving is partly offset by the single-program sort at 256 routes; inside the noise
T=128 keeps SGLang's op; drift control
T=256 keeps SGLang's op; drift control

companions.reason: Separates the hypothesis's two sub-changes. Control versus the parent (expert-id-map-single-kernel) gives the launch-fusion effect with Marlin seeing exactly SGLang's tensor extents. Primary versus control, in comparable runs, gives the 256->32 capacity effect on Marlin's m-block partition at small T, which the queued moe-align-local-expert-count can only probe at large T on a different base. Without it, any primary gain or loss at T<=32 could be either mechanism.

open_questions: Which path does sgl moe_align_block_size take at num_experts=256 and numel<=256 on the judge's image: the small-batch single kernel or the two-kernel align + count/sort path? Does the Python wrapper issue a separate sorted_ids.fill_ / cumsum zero? This sets whether the saving is 2 or 4 launches. Read the image's fused_moe_triton moe_align_block_size wrapper and sgl_kernel source before building.

Does moe_wna16_marlin_gemm compute its parallel m-block count from sorted_token_ids.size(0) (host capacity) or only read num_tokens_post_padded on the device? If the host capacity is used, the 256->32 shrink changes Marlin's tile striping on every T<=32 shape, and the control is essential.

What is the measured duration of the current align kernels and the new single-program kernel at T=32 (256 routes)? Pull them from the full per-kernel profile of the run, not the top-3 summary, and report them in the attribution.
Why was muse_moe_w4a16's 32-count master 3.2 us slower than SGLang's 256-count path at bs=1? If the capacity shrink is the cause, expect this primary to underperform the control at decode_1.

Comparison base: report the T<=32 deltas against the parent's result (expert-id-map-single-kernel, job with impl 08e8fcb6) as well as against BEST. The parent showed a uniform +1-2.5% shift that is likely drift.
